title: Alix Earle Debuts Netflix Series, Reveals Feud with Alex Cooper
seoTitle: Alix Earle's Netflix Debut: Feud with Alex Cooper Revealed
subtitle: The new series ‘Earle Meets World’ details the fallout with podcaster Alex Cooper
excerpt: Alix Earle has landed on Netflix with ‘Earle Meets World,’ where the influencer explains her split with Alex Cooper and reveals the behind-the-scenes of her Unwell.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Alix Earle debuted her reality show ‘Earle Meets World’ on Netflix, and already in the first episode, she addressed the dispute she had with podcaster Alex Cooper. The broadcast, scheduled for September 4th, has just become a trending topic for bringing to light details of the breakup that ended their partnership at Unwell Network.

What the series reveals about the feud with Alex Cooper

On the show, Earle describes a feeling of betrayal, saying that Cooper "sold her a dream" of protection that ultimately revealed itself as manipulation. She recounts that, at 22, she enthusiastically joined the "Call Her Daddy" podcast but ended up feeling used and "mistreated."

How the Unwell Network exit happened

Earle explains that upon joining Unwell, she lacked technical support – no producers, camera crew, or lighting – and that, although she managed to hire her own team, she still felt a lack of network support. According to her account, the network's team stopped inviting her to events and meetings.

Alex Cooper’s reactions and the social media atmosphere

In April 2026, Cooper responded to Earle in a TikTok video, accusing her of creating "fake drama" and spreading a "false narrative" about the feud. Earle replied to the comment with a simple "Okay on it."

The family's presence in the reality show

Alix's father, TJ, who runs a construction company in New Jersey, appears alongside his daughter, acting as her "dadager." He comments that the internet "was on fire" after her network exit and that the series tries to clarify the truth. Siblings, sister, and stepmother Ashley are also featured, bringing dynamism to the show.

Audience expectations and Netflix's strategy

With over 8.5 million followers on TikTok and 6 million on Instagram, Netflix is betting that Earle's fanbase will boost the premiere of the eight-episode series. The Vice President of Nonfiction Series, Brandon Riegg, described the premiere night as "very auspicious" and highlighted the influencer's confidence in telling her story to the public.

With information from USA Today, Deadline.
